rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - 2016 field experiment in Kailu County with TDR soil water measurements in a flood-irrigated plot and a mulched-drip plot, plus Hydrus-2D simulation. Q2: Section 3.2/Table 4/Figure 4 - model calibrated on flood-irrigation and validated on mulched-drip soil water measurements (NSE 0.35-0.86); Section 3.3/Table 5 - simulated drainage at bottom boundary 55.8 mm under flood vs 20.4 mm under mulched drip; Section 3.4.1/Figure 5 - cumulative water fluxes at 1.5-4.0 m under flood 1.8-2.8 times those under mulched drip; Section 3.4.2/Figure 6 - infiltration depth 400 cm under flood vs 325 cm under mulched drip; Abstract/Conclusions - mulched drip reduced infiltration depth and groundwater recharge. Q4: Table 5 and Figure 5 quantify the water-balance pathway (irrigation 381 vs 228 mm, evaporation 130.6 vs 60.2 mm, drainage, fluxes at successive depths) and Figure 3 reports measured profile soil water content, i.e. the intermediate variables linking irrigation method to reduced deep percolation.
rows.notes: Technology tested is drip combined with plastic film mulch versus flood; the mulch is confounded with drip, and the lower applied water (228 vs 381 mm) follows local practice, so the result is about the mulched-drip package rather than drip alone; counted as in scope since drip is the core technology but doubt noted. Recharge itself is not measured: it is a model output (drainage/flux) from Hydrus-2D validated only against soil water content to 150 cm; water table at 6.1 m is below the 4 m domain. Q3 no: measured soil water and the calibrated model are not independent methods. Q5 no: one site, one crop (maize), one season (2016). Q6 no: point profiles in centre of two ~70-86 ha fields with 2D domain of 180 cm; regional implications are extrapolated. Q7 no: growth-stage dependence is a variation, not a stated requirement. Q8 no: no explicit limitations beyond hedging ('to some extent'); authors argue post-harvest trend persists rather than stating a limitation. Q9 no: fluxes and drainage given as single values; MAE/NRMSE/NSE are validation errors, no SD/CI.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.3 - own 2016 field experiment (TDR soil water, auger samples, weather station) in two plots in Kailu County and Hydrus-2D modelling. Q2: Table 5 - simulated bottom drainage 20.4 mm under mulched drip vs 55.8 mm under flood; Figure 5 - cumulative fluxes at 1.5-4.0 m lower under mulched drip (9.6-2.0 cm vs 17.6-5.6 cm); Figure 6 - infiltration depth 325 vs 400 cm; model validated against measured soil water (Table 4, Figure 4); Section 4.2 and Conclusions - authors state mulched drip reduced recharge, lowering the water table and threatening stability of regional groundwater. Q4: Table 5 water balance (irrigation, evaporation, root uptake, drainage), Figure 5 depth-wise fluxes and Figure 3 measured profile soil water content trace the mechanism from irrigation method to reduced deep percolation.
rows.notes: The study's own result is reduced simulated deep drainage/infiltration depth at a single plot; the 'negative implications for regional groundwater stability' in the passage is the authors' inference in Discussion 4.2 and Conclusions, not a measured regional effect (no groundwater-level data reported). Technology is drip plus plastic mulch with lower applied water vs flood, so mulch and water amount are confounded with drip. Q3 no: single modelling chain calibrated on the same soil water data. Q5 no: one site, crop and season. Q6 no: plot-scale profiles and a 180 cm x 400 cm 2D domain; regional scale is extrapolation. Q7 no: no stated requirement from own findings. Q8 no: no explicit limitation statement. Q9 no: single-value outputs, only validation error statistics.

notes: Full text appears complete (text has duplicated/garbled lines from two-column OCR but all sections, tables and conclusions are legible). Study compares mulched drip irrigation (drip + plastic film) with flood irrigation for maize in one 2016 season at one site; groundwater recharge is inferred from Hydrus-2D drainage and flux outputs validated against measured soil water content to 150 cm, not from measured recharge or water-table data.
